name: push
documentation: Device-token registration and push delivery over APNs (HTTP/2, ES256 provider tokens) and FCM HTTP v1 (RS256 service-account tokens), with per-recipient fan-out, a delivery outbox and automatic pruning of tokens the provider reports dead.
//retry: max 1 on purpose. The OUTBOX owns retries, because it is the only place that knows whether a row was already delivered; a job-level retry would re-POST a notification the provider may already have accepted, and a duplicate push cannot be taken back.
//config: Every APNs and FCM credential is `required: false` WITH NO DEFAULT, which seeds a project's .env with `# KEY=` — commented out. That spelling is deliberate and was got wrong first: a BARE STRING entry means required-with-no-default, which writes an ACTIVE `KEY=`, and ValidateConfigStage counts '' as missing — so the boot of every project using FCM alone would stop on the unset APNs keys. `ground probe` is what caught it. ValidateConfigStage is static and cannot know that PUSH_APNS_* only matters when PUSH_APNS_ENABLED is true, so the check belongs where the decision is known: PushConfig::assertApnsUsable() and assertFcmUsable() refuse a half-configured provider and name the absent key.
//no-token-ttl-knob: There is deliberately no setting for the provider-token lifetime. Apple states the window: 'Refresh your token no more than once every 20 minutes and no less than once every 60 minutes.' A knob here has one correct range and two ways to earn a 429 TooManyProviderTokenUpdates, so the value is derived from the spec and not offered.
